annotationRationale: Prime exponent pairs encode distinct products, the multiplication principle counts the candidate pairs, and complement counting removes the four impossible products.
sourceMethod: Followed the official exponent-pair count and its four constructive cases, explicitly checking distinctness and why products are not counted twice.

review.mathCheck: Since 100000=2^5·5^5, products have 121 distinct exponent pairs in {0,…,10}². Exactly the four corners force equal factors. Each table row supplies valid unequal divisors for every other pair in its range, so there are 121-4=117 products, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful adaptation of MAA 10B solution 19 on page 9. Original explanatory prose and a table reproduce the official exponent count, four exclusions and four constructive factorizations.
review.annotationCheck: The solution counts distinct products rather than factor pairs and proves both uniqueness of the encoding and attainability. The assessed/support assignments fit.
